heading: 1 Summary of Inputs
text: featureMSEA requires three inputs: feature table LC-MS experiment, MS1 metabolite database annotation, metabolite set database enrichment testing.

heading: 1.1 Feature Table
text: feature table primary input can provided either .rda file (containing data frame) .csv file. row represents one metabolic feature detected LC-MS experiment. following columns required:Note condition: featureMSEA ranks features descending order condition value running enrichment, features larger values ranked higher contribute strongly enrichment score. condition column contain absolute value phenotype-associated statistic, |SNR|, |log₂FC|, |correlation coefficient|. magnitude-based ranking used, featureMSEA identifies metabolite sets collectively dysregulated, without distinguishing directionally - -regulated signals.

heading: 1.2 Reference Databases
text: Two reference databases required.MS1 metabolite database — used accurate-mass-based feature annotation (m/z matching). Supported options:KEGGHMDBMetabolite set database — defines sets metabolites tested enrichment. Supported options:

heading: 2 Annotation and Filtering
text:
Step 1, metabolic features annotated MS1 database via accurate mass matching within user-specified tolerance window. Co-eluting features sharing similar retention times grouped Metabolic Feature Clusters (MFCs), grouping strategy improves annotation confidence reduces redundancy resulting annotation table.

heading: 3 featureMSEA Analysis
text:
Step 2 performs feature rank-based metabolite set enrichment scoring. Features ranked according user-provided phenotype-associated statistic, metabolite set, running enrichment score computed across ranked feature list evaluate whether features annotated metabolites set non-randomly concentrated toward top ranking.

text: Note: Increasing Permutations improves p-value precision increases runtime proportionally. 1000 permutations gives good balance exploratory analysis; use 10,000+ publication-quality results.Click Run Step 2. heading: 4 LLM-assisted Interpretation
text:
Step 3 optional module uses Large Language Models (LLMs) evaluate biological plausibility enriched metabolite sets identified Step 2.
Figure 4.1: LLM evaluation interface

heading: 4.1.1 Matrix Confidence Assessment
text: Scores biological plausibility enriched metabolite set within specified biological sample matrix.Input: Biological matrix type (e.g., "urine", "plasma", "serum", "blood", "feces")Output: Per-metabolite-set matrix confidence score (0–100) reflecting whether metabolite set represents coherent biologically plausible biochemical entity within specified sample matrix

heading: 4.1.2 Topic Relevance Assessment
text: Searches PubMed scores enriched metabolite set based published evidence linking specific research context.Input: Research topic (e.g., "type 2 diabetes", "colorectal cancer", "pregnancy")Output: Per-metabolite-set topic relevance score supporting PubMed literature (PMIDs)
